Notification of Change of Residence (Change of Registered Information)
If not reported within the specified period, a fine will be imposed.
Application Period: Within 14 days from the date of change
Application Method: Apply in person at the immigration office (make a reservation through HiKorea)
Materials required: Completed Application Form, Passport, Alien Registration Card, and documents providing evidence of the change of registered information (e.g., lease agreement).
Time-based Employment Permit
If caught after failing to report entry or exit, you may face fines and be subject to forced deportation.
Target: D-2 and D-4 visa-holding international students (D-4 visa holders are eligible for a permit six months after entry).
Permitted Fields: Translation and interpretation, assisting in food service and duty-free shops, general office assistance, tourist information assistance, etc. (Manufacturing is not allowed).
Permitted Hours
Language training: Up to 25 hours per week
Undergraduate programs: Up to 30 hours per week
Master's and doctoral programs: Up to 35 hours per week
Degree program students (undergraduate, master's, and doctoral students) are exempt from weekly hour limits during weekends (Saturday and Sunday) and vacation periods.
Language training (D-4 visa holders) is only eligible after 6 months of foreigner registration.
Application Method: Apply in person at the Immigration Office or online through Hi Korea (www.hikorea.go.kr).
Required Documents: Integrated application form, time-based employment certificate, copy of the employer's business registration, employment contract, passport, alien registration card, grade or attendance certificate, TOPIK certificate.
The time-based employment certificate requires the signature of the supervisor (bring the necessary documents when visiting for the signature).
Time-based employment is available to those with a minimum of TOPIK Level 2 for language training, TOPIK Level 3 for the first and second-year undergraduates, and TOPIK Level 4 for third and fourth-year undergraduates and master's/doctoral students (those without TOPIK qualifications should inquire separately).
Note: Students with an attendance rate below 90% in the previous semester and a GPA below C (2.0) may be denied.
